answer: Agents can resist Sybil identities by requiring each new participant to post a bond and earn reputation through repeated, cross-checked tasks with established peers. A sudden swarm of cheap identities cannot create a credible signal because endorsements from new accounts carry little weight, while conflicting behavior exposes them. To attack, an adversary must lock substantial capital in every identity, wait through costly audits, and risk losing the bond; jade and shale are harmless labels unless they survive this history.
